name: esp32_s3_zero
title: Waveshare ESP32-S3-Zero
description: A small ESP32-S3 board: 4 MB flash and 2 MB PSRAM in the chip, castellated holes, USB-C to the chip, a WS2812B, BOOT and RESET buttons, a ceramic antenna
notes: USB-C goes to the chip itself, GPIO 19 and 20 through 22 ohm: no USB bridge, the log comes on the USB Serial/JTAG port.
GPIO 21 drives the WS2812B and is pulled up to 3V3 by R1, 1 kOhm.
GPIO 43 reaches the TX hole through R6, 499 ohm.
GPIO 14 to 18, 38 to 42 and 45 come out on pads, not holes: 14, 15 and 16 on the front, the others on the back.
GPIO 19 and 20 (USB), 33 to 37, 46, 47 and 48 do not come out.

power.name: 5V
power.why: VBUS of the USB-C, also on the 5V hole.

P15.type: castellated holes, 2.54 mm, 18 along two edges

front.source: a photo by Anton of his board, 2026-11-02

back.source: a photo by Anton of his board, 2026-11-02

connectors.source: P15 and the test points of the schematic; the labels of the holes and the pads on the photos of both sides of Anton's board

chip.notes: ESP32-S3 (QFN56) revision 0.2. The marking FH4R2 is on the photo of the chip.

antenna.source: J1 of the schematic with its matching network, no connector; a ceramic chip on the photo

antenna_rssi.by: rssi_probe on Anton's desk, one access point on channel 1, 60 s each
antenna_rssi.notes: Median RSSI on foam, 0 degrees: -64 dBm; lying on the desk: -66 at 0 and -70 at 90 degrees. In the same place an ESP32 DevKit with an ESP-WROOM-32 on its pins gave -63 at 0 degrees, an ESP32-C6 Super Mini on foam -59 and -70.
